subject: Sales postcall: Acme integration recap
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Khan <samira@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Acme Security <security@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sales postcall: Acme integration recap

Hi Samira —

Thanks again for your time today. Wanted to capture the highlights and next steps so everyone has the same view. TL;DR: good fit on latency-sensitive customer support use cases; main asks are streaming + function-calling for actions, structured output for downstream routing, and an embeddings-based reranker for search relevance.

Pain points you called out:
- Current vector search is noisy for short customer transcripts; ranking needs to prioritize recency & agent metadata.
- Live agent assist requires sub-200ms token turnaround to be useful during typing.
- Instrumentation & auditability for sensitive PII flows (retention policy + audit logs).

Goals we heard:
1) Replace current embed+BM25 stack for support KB ranking with an embeddings+reranker flow to improve NPS and reduce resolution time.
2) Add a streaming assistant into the agent UI (low latency real-time suggestions).
3) Ensure all traffic for EU customers is pinned to EU regions and logs meet audit/export requirements.

Integration / product fit notes (from our side):
- SDK changes: you will likely want our streaming SDK (JS + Python) to (a) stream incremental tokens to the UI and (b) expose function-calling hooks for triggering canned actions (create ticket, insert template). We can provide a small code sample for both.
- Function calling: Redwood supports structured function outputs (JSON schemas) and deterministic tool-calling hooks. This should let you map assistant outputs directly to your ticketing APIs without heavy post-processing.
- Structured outputs: we recommend using Redwood's structured-output mode for entity + intent extraction at generation time (vs post-parse). This reduces false positives and simplifies downstream routing.
- Embeddings & reranking: we propose a two-stage flow — approximate ANN for candidate retrieval + a lightweight reranker model hosted on Redwood to score top-K with context (agent metadata, recency). We can run an A/B on a subset of users to measure lift.

Attachments I dropped in this thread: redwood-integration-arch.png (arch diagram), acme-eval-prompt-set.xlsx (sample prompts / evals). Also linking our standard SLA doc for reference.

Next steps / owners:
- Redwood -> Dev + Rishi to provide streaming SDK sample and function-calling example by Thu (9/16). (owner: dev_patel)
- Acme -> Share a short eval prompt set and 1 week of anonymized transcripts for a rerank pilot. (owner: Samira)
- Schedule a follow-up technical demo w/ engineering to walk through the streaming latency SLOs and deployment patterns. Proposed slot: Fri 9/17 10:00am PT.

If that aligns, I’ll send a calendar invite for the technical demo and loop in our solutions engineer.

Thanks —
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this captures everything well. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Streaming latency: when you say sub-200ms token turnaround, is that measured from request to first-token or per-token incremental latency? Our frontend has already built an optimistic UI and we care about both first-token latency and steady-state.

2) Function calling: can you share a short JS example that shows a function call emitting a ticket-create payload and how Redwood guarantees schema validation? We want to avoid doing heavy validation in the frontend.

3) Security: our security team will send a short questionnaire (SOC2 + export controls). Can you confirm who on Redwood we should route that to?

We’ll try to assemble 1 week of anonymized transcripts by EOD Thu — I’ll send via the secure drive link. Also the proposed Fri 9/17 10:00am PT time works for the demo.

Best,
Samira
Samira Khan | Head of Product, Acme Analytics
samira@acme.com
